title: FAIL refuses a schema whose rows MapFlattener flattens without ambiguity
rationale: The only exercise anywhere of EnrichedSchemaFlattener.checkCollision. It pins the asymmetry the corpus already records for the legacy path: the schema half refuses a document the row half handles perfectly, so the library has no single answer to 'is this document representable'. Refusing is defensible for a name destined to become a column, since backslash is illegal in Avro and SQL identifiers; what is not defensible is that the row half of the same library succeeds on the same document.
catchesBugClass: The collision guard becoming inert - the single most likely regression, and the exact failure AvroSchemaFlattener already suffered once when its guard compared each duplicate against itself and never fired. Also catches the exception TYPE degrading from SchemaFlattenException to a bare RuntimeException, since the rendering carries the simple class name.
cannotCatch: It cannot show what a caller should DO about the refusal. It depends on FidelityRender.thrown's 240-character truncation and on the message text, so a purely cosmetic reword turns it red for no behavioural reason - a deliberate cost of recording throws as comparable values, shared with every existing THROWN fixture.

predicted.detail: The enriched arm throws SchemaFlattenException naming both source paths; the MapFlattener arm produces two distinct, unambiguous row keys.

configDescription: assert ENRICHED_KEYSET vs MAP_FLATTENER, default FlattenOptions (FAIL)
